description:
# Calendars-server handler-side pre-check of `maxExpandedQueryDuration`

After JMAP-ic0j.31 adds `CalendarsLimits.max_expanded_query_duration_seconds` and the `CalendarsBackend::limits` trait method, handler `handle_calendar_event_query` should optionally consult `backend.limits(caller, &account_id).max_expanded_query_duration_seconds` and short-circuit with `expandDurationTooLarge` when `before - after` exceeds it, BEFORE invoking `query_calendar_events`. This is defense-in-depth per workspace AGENTS.md "Backend caps and limits"; the backend is and remains canonical.

The hold-up is that `UTCDate` (RFC 8620 §1.4 `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`) has no arithmetic helpers in `jmap-types`, and `jmap-calendars-server`'s sealed dep set excludes `chrono`. Two coherent paths:

  (a) Add a small dep-free epoch_seconds parser in `jmap-types::UTCDate` (5 numeric fields + days-from-month-table arithmetic + Julian-day adjustment for cross-year diffs). Pre-1.0 the new method is additive non-breaking. Workspace-wide benefit: every extension that needs UTCDate arithmetic (today: calendars-server `maxExpandedQueryDuration`; tomorrow: any availability-window enforcement) reuses it. Recommended.

  (b) Hand-roll the parser inside `crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/event.rs` as a private helper. Smaller blast radius but the workspace would end up with N copies of the same parser as more extensions land tz-aware caps.

Neither path crosses the sealed dep set. Path (a) is the better long-term shape.

Test pattern: pre-check fires when `filter.before - filter.after > limits.max_expanded_query_duration_seconds`; assert handler returns `expandDurationTooLarge` BEFORE the backend is dispatched (use a TrackingBackend that increments a query_calendar_events counter; assert counter == 0 on rejection path).

Filed during JMAP-ic0j.31 as the deliberate scope split: limits() + struct land first; arithmetic-bearing pre-check lands next.
title: Calendars-server handler-side pre-check of maxExpandedQueryDuration
